text:
jess: Heads-up — I ran an nsys capture during the prefetch/evict experiment and we're getting repeated cudaMalloc spikes during KV-cache refills. Spikes are ~20-40ms and align with large eviction bursts. Uploading timeline and quick notes.

samir: Oof. Can you share the nsys command and a short perfetto slice? Also what allocator config did the test use (pool vs native malloc)? :eyes: 

jess: Command I used:```nsys profile --output=evict_run --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --sample=cpu --capture-range=nvtx --force-overwrite -- python tools/bench_prefetch.py --model=gpt-small --iters=600 --prefetch=6```
Timeline excerpt attached (perfetto link): https://perfetto.local/evict_run/slice/42
Allocator env: REDWOOD_ALLOC_POOL=0 (default native), REDWOOD_KVCACHE_PREFETCH=1

alec: That matches a hypothesis we had — native cudaMalloc on small allocations during eviction storms kills tail latency. Did you capture heap samples or cudaMalloc stack traces?

jess: Yes, nsys heap sampling shows most mallocs coming from kv_cache::insert path, many small (~16-64KB) allocations. I grabbed a short stack snippet:```#0 cudaMalloc
#1 gpu_backend::blob_alloc
#2 kv_cache::insert_chunk
#3 kv_cache::prefetch_worker
#4 prefetch_loop```

marie: Interesting — fragmentation + repeated tiny allocations. In earlier runs using the pooled arena we didn't see that severity. Could be the arena handing off to device allocator when chunk sizes don't match. 

samir: Upload from perf-bot: perf-bot: trace uploaded to https://s3.redwood-internal/traces/evict_run.qdrep (nsys exported + perfetto UI).

alec: Can you repro locally with deterministic seed? If so, try toggling pool on:```export REDWOOD_ALLOC_POOL=1
export REDWOOD_ARENA_CHUNK_MB=32
python tools/bench_prefetch.py --model=gpt-small --iters=200 --prefetch=6```
Also try increasing chunk to 64MB. We want to see whether coalescing reduces the number of cudaMalloc calls.

jess: Did both. Results (short):
- pool=0, chunk N/A: sample p99 cudaMalloc latency ~38ms, alloc count 1.2k in 200 iters
- pool=1, chunk=32MB: p99 ~12ms, alloc count 420
- pool=1, chunk=64MB: p99 ~9ms, alloc count 230
Numbers are rough from nsys heap samples but clear trend.

marie: Nice. That implies fragmentation/fit mismatch causing many backend calls. Can we get an nvtx-annotated kernel timeline for the chunk boundary? I want to see cross-stream stalls.

samir: Pasted small perf snippet (nsys timeline filter):```nvtx:prefetch_start [t=12.3s]
cudaMemcpyAsync kv->device [t=12.30-12.34]
cudaMalloc 32KB [t=12.341]
kernel: scatter_prefix [t=12.342-12.355]
cudaFree 32KB [t=12.356]
...repeat 20x
nvtx:prefetch_end [t=12.40s]```
This correlates with small cudaMalloc/cudaFree pairs inside the prefetch window. Kernel bubbles match.

alec: Two actionable items: (1) short-term: surface a config that defaults pool=1 for prefetch path in our perf config; (2) mid-term: implement slab coalescing so small allocations reuse partially-used slabs instead of going to device allocator. I'll draft an RFC.

jess: I also tried a quick patch to force integer-packed slab sizes (align to 256KB) and reran: p99 dropped to ~7.5ms. Logged results in issue #2345 with trace links.

marie: Good. One more experiment: try enabling a small LRU of recycled small blocks instead of immediate free. It might avoid the allocator churn during eviction storms.

samir: Agreed. I'll prototype a tiny recycled-cache for <=64KB allocations and run overnight on the perf rig. If it looks good we can ship as a heuristic behind REDWOOD_ALLOC_POOL_TINY_CACHE=1.

jess: Thanks — filing the reproducer + nsys+perfetto artifacts in the ticket. TL;DR: eviction storms + native malloc = cudaMalloc spike tail; pooled arena + larger chunks or tiny-reuse cache reduces p99 substantially. :thumbsup:
